_measured: Re-swept 2026-08-29 at commit c4509d2 after js/overlay.js, sink/table.html, sink/overflow-menu.html and templates/table-page.html changed, which had turned every cell stale. RUN TWICE, AT 1280x720 AND AGAIN AT 1440x900, and every gate returned the same numbers at both. The one movement was on portal.html, where check-spacing’s noReference count went 10 to 9 because a class picked up a comparable reference at the wider width; its divergences were the same three. The first pass recorded a caveat that a width-only divergence would have been missed -- that caveat was wrong about its own cause and is retracted here: resize_window emulates a viewport independently of how wide the Browser pane is, scaling the picture down rather than the layout, so innerWidth and every media query really do evaluate at the emulated size. The width was a choice, never a limit. check-a11y ran in BOTH themes on all eight pages at both widths, asserted each time from the resolved --rux-field-hover token (#e8e8e8 white / #333333 g100). check-spacing and check-runtime-classes ran in white only, which is sound because neither reads a colour. check-rendered does both themes itself; check-behaviour passed 18 of 18 at both widths. THE SIX CONDITIONS: document focus verified per page via document.hasFocus() and, for check-a11y, via focusRingChecked in the returned object -- empty-state initially reported focusRingChecked FALSE and that reading was discarded and retaken, which is condition 1 catching exactly what it exists for. check-runtime-classes ran first on each untouched page. The pointer was parked off content and the hover chain recorded with every result; on the 1440 pass it was empty on six of the eight pages. TWO RED RUNS, both on the sink: removing a singleton class from the live DOM made check-runtime-classes report it stripped with its section and element, and restoring it cleared the report; the checkbox focus-ring recipe from the sink-check skill produced exactly the 12 findings that skill records. THE FIRST RED RUN ALSO FOUND A BLIND SPOT. Removing ONE of the six occurrences of overflow-menu__icon changed nothing, because check-runtime-classes compares SETS of class names: a class stripped from some but not all of its elements is invisible to it. Only a class that disappears from the page entirely is caught. NOT COVERED BY ANY OF THIS: nobody has LOOKED at the rendered pages this sweep. Five defects this project shipped passed every gate.

_portal: portal.html RENDERS THIS FILE, so recording a reading against it changes the page the reading was taken from. Readings are taken on the build immediately before the entry is written; chasing the fixed point would not terminate, and what differs between the two builds is table text, altering no rule the three gates apply. KNOWN GAP: portal.html is a pageTarget of those gates but is NOT in their `inputs`, so editing it does not age its own cells. That is deliberate and it is a compromise. `inputs` is per GATE, not per cell -- kitchen-sink.html already ages the templates' cells -- so adding a page regenerated on every verify would mark every browser cell stale on every build, including cells it has nothing to do with. The narrower fix is per-cell inputs, which is a redesign of the registry and a separate decision.
